c74object.name: evi_waveshaping
c74object.digest: A GenExpr file, part of 'evieve', for using via 'require()'
c74object.description:
evi_waveshaping.genexpr is a .genexpr file and is part of the 'evieve' Package.
It is for using in a gen.codebox~ or in another .genexpr file via the require() command.
By declaring require("evi_waveshaping.genexpr"); at the top of a codebox you can then access all of the functions included in this file.
About this File:
A very long time ago this was called 'stkr.waveshaping.genexpr'. A collection of memoryless nonlinearities for waveshaping etc. Note: all of these functions are naive and need antialiasing / resampling to be of any use. @see: 'evi_adaa.genexpr' for antiderivative antialiasing and 'evi_saturators.genexpr' for quasi oversampling.

entry.name: tanhLApprox ( )
entry.description:
Tanh Lambert approx, 2x faster than library tanh(). Excellent mathematical and sonic closeness to library tanh(). In general we use this one most often.
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Tanh, Approximate tanh() of input

entry.name: tanhAxA ( )
entry.description:
Wrapper for tanhLApprox(). Returns 'tanh(x / a) * a'
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
In 2: type=input: gain, ± linear gain, input div, output mul
Return 1: Tanh, Approximate tanh() of input wrapped by gain coefficient

entry.name: tanhSqrt ( )
entry.description:
A cheaper alternative to tanh, not exactly the same, I describe this as a 'buzzy tanh'
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Tanh, Approximate tanh() of input

entry.name: tanhPoly ( )
entry.description:
Another cheaper alternative to tanh, behaves differently at very high gain
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Tanh, Approximate tanh() of input

entry.name: atanApprox ( )
entry.description:
Atan() approximation, excellent sonic and mathematical closeness to library atan()
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Atan, Approximate atan() of input

entry.name: atanDrive ( )
entry.description:
Gain wrapping for 'atanApprox()'
In 1: type=input: drive, Linear drive control, 1++
Return 1: pre, Pre gain shaped
Return 2: post, Post gain shaped

entry.name: atanSat ( )
entry.description:
Full wrapping of 'atanApprox()' with 'atanDrive()' pre/post gain wrapping
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
In 2: type=input: drive, Linear drive control, 1++
Return 1: Atan, Saturated atan() output

entry.name: tarrabiaShaper ( )
entry.description:
Variable shaper, if 'a' is negative effect is cubic-like, if 'a' is positive effect is diode-like
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
In 2: type=input: a, Gain in range less than -1..1
Return 1: Shape, Shaped audio output

entry.name: jongShaper ( )
entry.description:
The greater the harmonics ('a') the more diode like in shape, but retains a very smooth curve
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
In 2: type=input: a, 1++, add harmonics
Return 1: Shape, Shaped audio output

entry.name: cubicNL ( )
entry.description:
Classic cubic nonlinearity, good for guitar-like sound worlds
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Cubic, Cubic distorted output

entry.name: thbNL ( )
entry.description:
Cubic nonlinearity, versatile
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Cubic, Cubic distorted output

entry.name: polyNom ( )
entry.description:
A lovely polynomial from Reaktor, unbounded
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Polynomial, Polynomial shaped output

entry.name: polySat ( )
entry.description:
You need to wrap the 'polyNom()' in something like this to make it bounded and thus usable
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Polynomial, Polynomial saturated output

entry.name: parabolSat ( )
entry.description:
Smooth parabolic saturation
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
In 2: type=input: a, Linear gain, default should be '1'
In 3: type=input: c, Linear clipping range, default should be '2'
Return 1: Parabol, Parabolic saturated output

entry.name: scDistort ( )
entry.description:
Simple shaper from SuperCollider, like the 'distort()' UnaryOp
In 1: type=input: x0, Audio input
In 2: type=input: drive, Linear drive, 0++
Return 1: Distort, Distorted output

entry.name: scSoftClip ( )
entry.description:
Simple soft clipper from SuperCollider, like the 'softclip()'/'fold2()' UnaryOps
In 1: type=input: x0, Audio input
In 2: type=input: drive, Linear drive, 0++
Return 1: Soft Clip, Soft clipped output

entry.name: raffelBBD ( )
entry.description:
Unbounded, does almost nothing (adds one harmonic when you need it), nice
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
Return 1: Shape, Shaped audio output

entry.name: localSinParam ( )
entry.description:
Create gain wrapping parameters for 'sinSat()'
In 1: type=input: drive, Drive amount % 0..1.. up to 2 is pretty safe, up to 4 be careful
Return 1: pidrive, Pre gain shaped
Return 2: sindrive, Post gain shaped

entry.name: sinSat ( )
entry.description:
Sine shaping saturation, gain wrapped
In 1: type=input: x, Audio input
In 2: type=input: drive, Drive amount % 0..1.. up to 2 is pretty safe, up to 4 be careful
Return 1: Sine, Sine shaped saturated output

entry.name: modHT ( )
entry.description:
A modified gain wrapping around a tanh-like saturation shape
In 1: type=input: x0, Audio input
In 2: type=input: d, Gain must be clipped 0..1
In 3: type=input: a, Drive must be clipped 1..10
Return 1: Tanh, Mapped tanh-like saturation

entry.name: foldBD ( )
entry.description:
A folding shape algorithm around a given threshold, works particularly well on low end frequency content
In 1: type=input: xin, Audio input
In 2: type=input: thresh, Saturation threshold 0.01..1, but best kept 0.5..1
Return 1: Fold, Folding shaped distortion output

entry.name: tapeH ( )
entry.description:
Morphing sigmoid, 'tape' curve == 'sigmoid' @ -5, tanh curve == 'sigmoid' @ -2
In 1: type=input: xin, Audio input
In 2: type=input: sigmoid, Negative produces saturation, can be driven very low for extreme shapes
Return 1: Tanh, Tanh-like saturator with increasingly strong harmonics

entry.name: gloubiBoulga ( )
entry.description:
The famous 'Gloubi Boulga' by Laurent de Soras, but it is very hard to anti-alias
In 1: type=input: x2, Audio input
In 2: type=input: drive, Linear gain 1..40 -ish
Return 1: Gloubi, Asymmetric clipping distortion

entry.name: boulgaStatic ( )
entry.description:
The famous 'Gloubi Boulga' by Laurent de Soras but in a static version slightly easier to anti-alias
In 1: type=input: xin, Audio input
Return 1: Boulga, Asymmetric clipping distortion
